title: test
summary: Return test-set masks from a cvpartition object.

gpu_support.notes: The partition metadata is host-side. A resident index is gathered through its owning provider, and the logical mask is restored to that same provider.

description: `test(c)` returns a logical test mask for single-test-set partitions. `test(c,i)` returns masks for selected K-fold, leaveout, or custom test sets.
behaviors: `test(c)` works for holdout, resubstitution, and custom partitions with one test-set column.
`test(c,i)` accepts a one-based single- or double-precision scalar or vector of test-set indices.
`test(c,'all')` returns one logical mask column per test set.
RunMat mode also accepts logical and all eight typed-integer index classes. Typed integers are decoded exactly as structural indices without conversion through double.
A resident index produces a resident logical mask owned by the same acceleration provider.
For resubstitution partitions, `test(c)` is all true because every observation is used for both training and testing.

examples.description: Get the test mask for one fold

faqs.question: How do I retrieve all test masks?
faqs.answer: Use `test(c,'all')`; columns correspond to test-set indices.

faqs.question: Can `i` be an integer array?
faqs.answer: In RunMat mode, yes. Every integer class is read exactly. MATLAB-compatible mode accepts the documented single- and double-precision index forms.

faqs.question: Does `test` preserve GPU residency?
faqs.answer: Yes. When `i` is resident, RunMat gathers it through its owning provider and restores the logical output to that provider.
